acceptance_criteria.criterion: AC-11b: Accepted options saved back via `SaveAsync` on dialog accept.
AC-11c: Parameterless constructor works with default options.
AC-12: Build zero warnings; all 613+ tests pass.

summary: Added SaveCallCount and LastSaved tracking properties to FakeSettingsService.
Added ToOptions() method to LabelCleanerViewModel returning current option state as LabelCleanerOptions.
Injected ISettingsService? into MovieEditorViewModel as optional constructor parameter.
Updated CleanLabel command to read _settingsService?.Current.LabelCleaner ?? new LabelCleanerOptions() as initialOptions.
After dialog accept, saves accepted options back via _settingsService.SaveAsync using immutable with { LabelCleaner = vm.ToOptions() } pattern.
Updated Program.cs MovieEditorViewModel DI factory to pass sp.GetRequiredService<ISettingsService>().

Added BuildSutWithCleanLabelAndSettings factory helper and 3 new unit tests: CleanLabel_PassesOptionsFromSettings_ToLabelCleanerViewModel, CleanLabel_SavesOptionsToSettings_OnDialogAccept, ParameterlessConstructor_CreatesValidVm_WithDefaultOptions.
Build: zero warnings. All 626 tests pass (235 App, 223 Core, 168 Infrastructure).

comments.note: LabelCleanerViewModel._keywords is a private IReadOnlyList<string> field that cannot be changed via the dialog UI. ToOptions() correctly captures it, but if future work adds a keyword editor to the dialog, the field will need to become mutable or be replaced with an ObservableCollection-backed property.

MovieEditorViewModel.CleanLabel silently no-ops when _settingsService is null but still accepts the dialog result and updates label/actor/studio fields. This is intentional by design (no-arg ctor path), but the silent SaveAsync skip could confuse future readers — a brief comment was already present in the WP spec making this explicit.

FakeSettingsService in tests/VideoIndexer.App.Tests/TestHelpers/FakeSettingsService.cs previously did not track call counts unlike other fakes in the same folder (e.g. FakeMovieRepository). Adding SaveCallCount and LastSaved brings it into alignment with the established pattern.

summary: All 4 acceptance criteria verified. Build: 0 warnings, 0 errors. Tests: 626 passed (223 Core, 235 App, 168 Infrastructure), 0 failed, 6 skipped (live DB). AC-11a confirmed: CleanLabel reads _settingsService?.Current.LabelCleaner ?? new LabelCleanerOptions() and passes options to LabelCleanerViewModel constructor. AC-11b confirmed: SaveAsync is called inside the if (result is not null) block with an immutable with { LabelCleaner = vm.ToOptions() } update. AC-11c confirmed: parameterless constructor leaves _settingsService null; CleanLabel early-exits safely via the null-guard. DI wiring in Program.cs passes sp.GetRequiredService<ISettingsService>() to the factory. AppOptions.LabelCleaner is non-nullable with = new() default — no null-ref risk.

comments.note: CleanLabel_SavesOptionsToSettings_OnDialogAccept only asserts SaveCallCount==1 and LastSaved!=null. It does not verify that LastSaved.LabelCleaner reflects the dialog's final option state. This is a minor gap; the logic is simple and correct, but a follow-up assertion on the actual property values would harden the regression net.

No explicit test for the discard path (result is null → SaveAsync NOT called). The code is correct (SaveAsync is inside if (result is not null)), but a dedicated test would prevent silent regressions if the guard is ever refactored.

No observations beyond the above — code is clean, immutable settings mutation follows the established with {} pattern, and FakeSettingsService is consistent with other fakes in the test helpers folder.

summary: Code review PASS with one Fix-Forward applied. All 4 ACs met. Architecture is clean: ISettingsService is correctly wired as an optional dependency, the immutable with{} AppOptions mutation pattern is followed, and the CleanLabel save guard correctly scopes the SaveAsync call inside `if (result is not null)`. Fix-Forward applied: strengthened AC-11b test to use custom LabelCleanerOptions and assert the actual property values persisted to LastSaved.LabelCleaner, making the regression net concrete rather than existence-only. 626 tests pass after the fix.

comments.note: Fix-Forward applied to CleanLabel_SavesOptionsToSettings_OnDialogAccept in MovieEditorViewModelTests.cs: added custom LabelCleanerOptions (UCWords=false, PreserveDates=false, StripKeywords=true) to the test setup and added three property-level assertions on settings.LastSaved!.LabelCleaner. The prior test only checked SaveCallCount==1 and LastSaved!=null, which would pass even if the wrong options were persisted. The strengthened assertions close that gap without changing any production code.

No discard-path test exists (CleanLabel called with result==null should NOT call SaveAsync). The production guard `if (result is not null)` is correct, but a dedicated test would prevent silent regressions if the guard is ever refactored. Recommend adding in a future pass.

CleanLabel uses `_settingsService.Current` as the base for the `with { LabelCleaner = ... }` update after the async dialog completes. In theory this is a TOCTOU window if settings could be mutated concurrently, but in a WinExe desktop app with a modal dialog this is not a reachable hazard. No action required.

[documentation-forward] LabelCleanerViewModel.ToOptions() is a new public method on the VM — add its signature, return type, and purpose (capturing current toggle state for settings persistence) to api-surface.md.

notes: All 4 acceptance criteria met. ISettingsService is now fully wired into MovieEditorViewModel for LabelCleaner options persistence. 3 new unit tests cover AC-11a/b/c. Build is zero-warning; 626 tests pass. Ready for QA.
All 4 ACs met. 626 tests pass, 0 failures. Two minor test coverage gaps noted (SaveAsync options content not asserted; discard path not tested) — neither is a hard failure. Ready for code review.
